newsitem.title: USA: Virginia Power sees Surry 1 back by weekend.
newsitem.headline: Virginia Power sees Surry 1 back by weekend.

text.p: Virginia Power said Thursday its 781 megawatt (MW) Surry 1 nuclear power unit would likely resume operation by this weekend after it was shut late Wednesday for electrical repairs.
"We anticipate the unit returning by the weekend," said a company spokesman.
He said plant engineers shut Surry unit 1 at about 2300 EST Wednesday after detecting a pressure drop in the reactor coolant system.
Findings showed a failure with the system's controller, an electronic device that governs pressure inside the system.
"We're repairing that controller...It's going to take most of the day," the spokesman said.
Meanwhile, the adjoining Surry 2 unit, also at 781 MW, is expected to return on line Friday, he added.
Surry 2 was taken off line Tuesday after losing power in its electrical hydraulic control system.

The outage of both Surry units in Gravel Neck, Va., would not affect power deliveries to customers due to the current mild weather and moderate energy demand in its service territory, the spokesman said.
Virginia Power is a subsidiary of Dominion Resources.
